control_device_fabrication: The PSCs demonstrated a champion PCE of 14.979%, with a VOC of 1.0221 V, JSC of 19.448 mA/cm², and FF of 75.357%. The Cs0.05MA0.16FA0.79I2.9Br0.1 perovskite precursor (1.73 mol/L) was spin-coated onto the substrate. Controlled addition of MeO-4PADBC (0.33 mg/mL) as a SAM was performed to stabilize the perovskite layer and engineer a more robust interface.  The perovskite solutions were spin-coated at 1000 rpm for 10 s (acceleration rate 500 rpm/s) and 5000 rpm for 30 s (acceleration rate 1000 rpm/s), respectively. 160 µL of antisolvent was dropped on the film 6 s before the end of the program. The perovskite film was annealed at 110 °C for 25 min.
target_device_fabrication: Remarkably, it achieved an impressive PCE of 16.2254% with a high VOC of 0.964507 V, JSC of 24.0563 mA/cm², and FF of 69.9298%. The perovskite precursor solution (1.73 mol/L) was prepared in mixed solvents of DMF and DMSO according to chemical formula of Cs0.05MA0.16FA0.79I2.9Br0.1. A SAM solution consisting of MeO-4PADBC (0.33 mg/mL) in ethanol was prepared. During solar cell device fabrication, MACl (5.0 mg/mL) was added to the precursor solution. A sequential spin-coating procedure was employed, first at 1000 rpm for 10 s, followed by 5000 rpm for 30 s. During this stage, 160 µL CB antisolvent was quickly dripped onto the centre of the substrate at 6 s before the end of the spin-coating process. A precise annealing regimen (110 °C, 25 min) refined the perovskite microstructure.
